column1: What are the three architectural invariants embodied by the Linux monolithic kernel design?
column2: Isolation (userspace cannot access kernel memory/I/O directly), Abstraction (hardware diversity hidden behind uniform interfaces), and Efficiency (single address space minimizes context-switch overhead).

column1: In the Linux task_struct, what does 'vruntime' represent and which data structure tracks it for scheduling?
column2: vruntime is the virtual runtime used by CFS to track proportional CPU time consumed; it is tracked in a per-CPU red-black tree (struct rb_root_cached) with the leftmost node cached for O(1) selection of the next task to run.

column1: What happens to a task's vruntime when it wakes from sleep in CFS, and why?
column2: It is set to min_vruntime (the current minimum across all runnable tasks) to prevent the task from monopolizing the CPU after waking, since sleeping tasks would otherwise retain an artificially low vruntime.

column1: What is the 'Durability Ordering' invariant in filesystem design?
column2: Observable state transitions must respect dependency ordering — metadata pointing to data must not become durable before the data itself reaches stable storage (preventing dangling references after a crash).

column1: What subtle POSIX semantic does 'delayed allocation' in modern filesystems break?
column2: It breaks the implicit guarantee that successful write() reserves space — because blocks are allocated only at writeback time, space exhaustion can occur after write() succeeds but before fsync().

column1: Why did Linux 3.6 remove the IPv4 route cache?
column2: Because under adversarial traffic patterns it caused unbounded memory growth; the FIB trie (LC-trie/Patricia trie) structure made per-packet FIB lookups fast enough (O(W), W=address width) without needing a cache.

column1: Why does PAWS (Protection Against Wrapped Sequences) matter on modern high-speed links?
column2: TCP's 32-bit sequence number space wraps in ~3.4 seconds on a 10 Gbps link; PAWS uses the TCP timestamp option to disambiguate reordered segments from earlier connection incarnations, making it non-optional on modern hardware.

column1: How does IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP) improve scalability over IPv4 ARP?
column2: NDP uses ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicitation/Advertisement sent to solicited-node multicast addresses instead of ARP's layer-2 broadcasts, reducing unnecessary interruption of unrelated hosts on the network.

column1: What is the fundamental invariant distinguishing pathnames from inodes in a Unix filesystem?
column2: Pathnames are ephemeral namespace entries, while inodes are the persistent file objects representing true file identity; multiple pathnames (hard links) can reference the same inode, which persists until its reference count reaches zero.

column1: What is the Block Allocation Invariant in filesystem design?
column2: A block can belong to at most one file or metadata structure at any time; violation causes catastrophic corruption where unrelated files share storage.

column1: What is the core difference between full virtualization and paravirtualization regarding privileged instructions?
column2: Full virtualization (KVM, Xen HVM) uses hardware extensions (VT-x/AMD-V) to trap and emulate privileged instructions transparently; paravirtualization (Xen PV) modifies the guest kernel to issue explicit hypercalls instead of privileged instructions.

column1: What is the invariant guaranteed by containerization versus virtualization regarding the kernel?
column2: Containers: all processes share and see the same single host kernel but perceive different namespace-isolated views of resources (PIDs, network, filesystem). Virtualization: each guest runs its own distinct kernel with separate page tables managed by the hypervisor.
